§9.8.2 Triangles and Matrix Tables

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-triangles-and-matrix-tables · tables encoding empty-cells

✅ Normative

Every row MUST carry the full column count. The jagged half MUST be padded with individual empty cells — one <td></td> per missing position. A colspan or rowspan over the empty region MUST NOT be used, and a 0 or any other value MUST NOT be invented.

Loss development exhibits and similar matrices are jagged on purpose. The missing half is meaningfully empty — that development period has not happened yet — not data that failed to be read.

Accident yr | 12mo | 24mo | 36mo |
| 2021      | 450  | 512  | 530  |
| 2022      | 470  | 528  |      |  ← structurally empty,
| 2023      | 465  |      |      |    not "failed to read"

Requirements

  • The shape MUST be kept. Every row has the full column count; the cells past the end of the row are present and empty. Rows MUST NOT be truncated.
  • One empty cell per missing position. Four unhappened periods are four <td></td>, not one colspan="4". The span would say "this region is one thing", and it is not — it is four distinct coordinates that each have not happened yet.
  • The empty half MUST NOT be padded with values. Filling it with 0, n/a or a repeat of the last figure destroys the only thing the triangle asserts.
  • A printed value MUST NOT be read as structural emptiness either. Some pages print 0 across the future half. A zero is a claim and a blank is an absence; the output MUST render whichever the page prints.
  • A cell that is empty because it cannot be read is a different situation — see Cell Text Fidelity§9.6.3.

✅ Sample — ppy

Stacked loss-development exhibits where the empty lower-right is meaningfully empty: those development periods have not happened. Every row of the first triangle carries all eleven cells. The column headers are underlined, not bold.

Why a span is wrong here, when it is free elsewhere

Blank and Spacer Rows§9.5.1 leaves the encoding of an unruled empty region free: leading empty cells and one blank spanning block render identically, and neither is preferred.

A triangle is the carve-out. Every empty cell sits at a real coordinate — an accident year crossed with a development period — and "12 months has not elapsed for the 2023 year" is a separate fact from the same statement about 24 months. Collapsed into one span, those coordinates stop being addressable: a consumer can no longer ask what the 2023 row holds at 24 months, because the cell it would look in no longer exists.

Elsewhere the empty region is one undifferentiated blank. Here it is a set of individually meaningful absences that happen to be adjacent.

This is the same principle that settles blank space beside a header in Barely-Existing Columns and Headers§9.3.1: a span is a claim that the page merged something. The page did not merge these.

Why the blank matters more here than elsewhere

In most tables, blank versus an explicit empty marker is cosmetic. In a loss triangle the blank carries actuarial meaning: it asserts this development period does not exist yet, which is a fact about the world, not a gap in the transcription. That is the same argument that makes the em-dash a value in Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6 and the coloured fill a value in Color as the Value§9.6.4 — a non-value that is a value.
